ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a large dictionary is placed on a table, with a sheet of A4 paper (whose mass and thickness are negligible) inserted deep into the dictionary. Assume the mass of the dictionary is uniformly distributed, and the pressure distribution on the same page is also uniform. The total mass of the dictionary is $M=1.5\,\mathrm{kg}$, its width is $L=16\,\mathrm{cm}$, and its height is $H=6\,\mathrm{cm}$. The kinetic friction coefficient between the upper and lower surfaces of the A4 paper and the pages of the dictionary is $\mu_{1}=0.3$, and the kinetic friction coefficient between the dictionary and the table is $\mu_{2}$. The maximum static friction force on each contact surface is approximately equal to the sliding friction force. When the A4 paper is pulled horizontally to the right and is inserted at a height $h=2\,\mathrm{cm}$ from the table surface, the dictionary is just able to be moved. The gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the dictionary and the desktop is $\mu_{2}$.
2. If an A4 paper is placed at the deepest part of a dictionary and is at a height of $3cm$ from the table surface, and a horizontal rightward force $F$ is applied to pull the A4 paper out of the dictionary at a constant speed, write the functional expression of the force $F$ with respect to the displacement $x$ of the A4 paper (during the process of pulling out the A4 paper, only the part of the dictionary overlapping with the upper side of the A4 paper exerts pressure on the A4 paper). Do not add any additional content.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a thick dictionary is placed on a tabletop, and a sheet of white A4 paper is horizontally inserted into the inside of the dictionary, dividing the dictionary into upper and lower parts; the paper extends outward, and the horizontal width/overlap length L of the dictionary along the pulling-out direction is marked at the bottom. Reasoning: The dictionary has uniform mass, total mass M=1.5 kg, and height H=6 cm. When the paper insertion height is h=2 cm, the mass proportion of the dictionary part above the paper is (H-h)/H, so the normal pressure received by each side of the paper is taken as N=Mg(H-h)/H according to the specified concentrated model. Both the upper and lower surfaces of the paper have friction with the dictionary, so the resultant horizontal friction force transmitted by the paper to the dictionary is 2μ1N. When the dictionary can just be driven, this force is equal to the maximum static friction force μ2Mg exerted by the table on the whole dictionary, therefore μ2Mg=2μ1Mg(H-h)/H, giving μ2=2×0.3×(6-2)/6=0.4. In the second question, the paper is at a height of 3 cm, namely the mass of the dictionary above is M/2; the remaining overlap length is L-x, and the pressure on the same page is uniform, so the normal pressure exerted on the paper by the upper overlapping part is (Mg/2)(L-x)/L. When the paper is pulled out at constant speed, the pulling force balances the sliding friction forces on the upper and lower surfaces, so F=2μ1·(Mg/2)(L-x)/L=μ1Mg(L-x)/L.

method.method_draft: Use a lumped free-body analysis of the two book portions separated by the paper. First read the figure as a dictionary resting on a table with an A4 sheet inserted horizontally between upper and lower pages; the marked length L is the horizontal book width/overlap length. From the text use uniform mass distribution, M=1.5 kg, H=6 cm, h=2 cm, mu1=0.3, and the condition that the book is just about to move. The paper supports the weight of the upper part of the dictionary, so at insertion height h the normal force on each face of the paper is N=Mg(H-h)/H. Because the paper contacts pages on both its upper and lower faces, the rightward friction transmitted to the dictionary is 2mu1N. At the threshold this equals the maximum table friction mu2 Mg, giving mu2=2mu1(H-h)/H=0.4. For the second part, at height 3 cm the upper mass is M/2; with uniform pressure and remaining overlap L-x, the normal due to the upper overlapping part is (Mg/2)(L-x)/L. The pulling force at constant speed balances friction on both paper faces: F=2mu1(Mg/2)(L-x)/L=mu1Mg(L-x)/L.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中一本厚字典放在桌面上，一张白色A4纸水平插入字典内部，把字典分成上下两部分；纸张向外伸出，底部标出了字典沿拉出方向的水平宽度/重叠长度L。推理：字典质量均匀，总质量M=1.5 kg，高度H=6 cm。纸插入高度h=2 cm时，纸上方字典部分质量占比为(H-h)/H，所以纸每一面受到的正压力按指定集中模型取N=Mg(H-h)/H。纸的上下两面都与字典有摩擦，因此纸传给字典的水平摩擦合力为2μ1N。字典刚能被带动时，该力等于桌面对整本字典的最大静摩擦力μ2Mg，因此μ2Mg=2μ1Mg(H-h)/H，得μ2=2×0.3×(6-2)/6=0.4。第二问中纸在3 cm高度，即上方字典质量为M/2；剩余重叠长度为L-x，且同页压力均匀，因此上方重叠部分对纸的正压力为(Mg/2)(L-x)/L。纸匀速拉出时，拉力平衡上下两面的滑动摩擦力，所以F=2μ1·(Mg/2)(L-x)/L=μ1Mg(L-x)/L。

method.method_draft: Use a distributed pressure/friction-density model. From the image, identify the paper as a flat sheet extending through the dictionary, with the book-pages contact region spanning length L. From the text, use uniform mass and uniform pressure, so the vertical load per unit overlap length from the material above the sheet is proportional to the height of dictionary above the sheet. For h=2 cm, the overlying fraction is (H-h)/H=4/6; the total downward load per full-length contact is Mg(H-h)/H. The shear force density on each paper face is mu1 times the corresponding pressure; integrating over both faces gives total rightward shear on the dictionary 2mu1Mg(H-h)/H. Equate this to the table resisting friction mu2Mg at the moment the dictionary just moves to obtain mu2=0.4. For h=3 cm, the overlying fraction is 1/2, but during withdrawal only length L-x still overlaps the upper book portion. Integrate the same shear density only over the remaining overlap: F=2mu1[Mg/2][(L-x)/L]=mu1Mg(L-x)/L.

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, a large dictionary is placed on a table, with a sheet of A4 paper (whose mass and thickness are negligible) inserted deep into the dictionary. Assume the mass of the dictionary is uniformly distributed, and the pressure distribution on the same page is also uniform. The total mass of the dictionary is $M=1.5\,\mathrm{kg}$, its width is $L=16\,\mathrm{cm}$, and its height is $H=6\,\mathrm{cm}$. The kinetic friction coefficient between the upper and lower surfaces of the A4 paper and the pages of the dictionary is $\mu_{1}=0.3$, and the kinetic friction coefficient between the dictionary and the table is $\mu_{2}$. The maximum static friction force on each contact surface is approximately equal to the sliding friction force. When the A4 paper is pulled horizontally to the right and is inserted at a height $h=2\,\mathrm{cm}$ from the table surface, the dictionary is just able to be moved. The gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the dictionary and the desktop is $\mu_{2}$.
2. If an A4 paper is placed at the deepest part of a dictionary and is at a height of $3cm$ from the table surface, and a horizontal rightward force $F$ is applied to pull the A4 paper out of the dictionary at a constant speed, write the functional expression of the force $F$ with respect to the displacement $x$ of the A4 paper (during the process of pulling out the A4 paper, only the part of the dictionary overlapping with the upper side of the A4 paper exerts pressure on the A4 paper). Do not add any additional content.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a thick dictionary is placed on a tabletop, and a sheet of white A4 paper is horizontally inserted into the inside of the dictionary, dividing the dictionary into upper and lower parts; the paper extends outward, and the horizontal width/overlap length L of the dictionary along the pulling-out direction is marked at the bottom. Reasoning: The dictionary has uniform mass, total mass M=1.5 kg, and height H=6 cm. When the paper insertion height is h=2 cm, the mass proportion of the dictionary part above the paper is (H-h)/H, so the normal pressure received by each side of the paper is taken as N=Mg(H-h)/H according to the specified concentrated model. Both the upper and lower surfaces of the paper have friction with the dictionary, so the resultant horizontal friction force transmitted by the paper to the dictionary is 2μ1N. When the dictionary can just be driven, this force is equal to the maximum static friction force μ2Mg exerted by the table on the whole dictionary, therefore μ2Mg=2μ1Mg(H-h)/H, giving μ2=2×0.3×(6-2)/6=0.4. In the second question, the paper is at a height of 3 cm, namely the mass of the dictionary above is M/2; the remaining overlap length is L-x, and the pressure on the same page is uniform, so the normal pressure exerted on the paper by the upper overlapping part is (Mg/2)(L-x)/L. When the paper is pulled out at constant speed, the pulling force balances the sliding friction forces on the upper and lower surfaces, so F=2μ1·(Mg/2)(L-x)/L=μ1Mg(L-x)/L.
